title: Monitoring and adapting endurance training on the basis of heart rate variability monitored by wearable technologies: A systematic review with meta-analysis
authors: Düking P, Zinner C, Trabelsi K, Reed J, Holmberg H, Kunz P, Sperlich B
journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
population: Endurance-training adults in 8 studies comparing HRV-guided with predefined training (9 interventions)
findings: 8 studies (198 participants) and 9 interventions were meta-analysed; PubMed and Web of Science were searched in March 2020.
Compared with predefined training, most HRV-guided interventions included fewer moderate- and/or high-intensity training sessions.
Fixed-effects meta-analysis: significant medium-sized positive effect of HRV-guided training on submaximal physiological parameters (g = 0.296, 95% CI 0.031 to 0.562, p = 0.028).

Effects on performance (g = 0.079, p = 0.597) and VO2peak (g = 0.171, 95% CI -0.213 to 0.371, p = 0.130) were small and not statistically significant. The abstract's performance CI (-0.050 to 0.393) does not bracket g = 0.079, an apparent typo in the source.
With regard to performance, HRV-guided training was associated with fewer non-responders and more positive responders.
limitations: Only 8 small studies using a variety of HRV approaches; fixed-effects model; short interventions; the abstract does not describe sex or training level of participants; the abstract contains an internally inconsistent CI.
implications: HRV guidance behaves as a risk-reduction layer, not a performance enhancer: use it to withhold or downgrade hard sessions, not to add load.

Keep the planned session as the default and let HRV only convert a planned moderate/high session to easy on flagged days. HRV-guided arms did fewer hard sessions with equal or better outcomes, so skipped intensity need not be made up.
Do not present HRV as improving race performance; no change to periodisation is justified by this evidence.

verification.notes: Crossref: title, journal, first author Düking, issued Nov 2021 all match. Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34489178) states every number. Removed the researcher's unsupported 'mostly recreational/trained males' limitation.
